tweets.text: RT @llamaonthebrink: Blockchains are append-only data structures made for use cases that are non-reversible or immutable. Permissionless money is the most obvious use case for that system. A less obvious use case is a public contract. Contracts, once in effect, are meant to be unalterable. Onchain immutability truly enhances the properties of a contract. Onchain messaging, communication, socials, or other plain language objects haven’t taken off because they don’t benefit from an append-only platform. The ability to edit and delete a message is a basic feature of any messaging or social app. But not for contracts. The ability to alter a contract is a major bug. Trueo makes unique use of the chain by using it as an immutable message board for plain language contracts. The event contracts themselves are posted as human readable strings inside transaction call data. Set in stone. Never to be altered or deleted. The original lives inside someone’s node forever. A symbol of immutability and a display of how blockchain’s can be practically used beyond direct financial transactions.
